about: P64 T8-R3 dev set for board genres: 16 new English sentences written 29. 10. 2026 after the sealed P64 set was opened. The sealed set showed board genres losing their scene on a portrait phone, and p30/dev.json has almost no board genre. Two sentences each for the four genres that lost (timing, slice, catch, merge), one for every other board genre. genre = what the quick game's offline classifier picks today (classifyGenre(text, null).ranked[0].genre). Tuning happens here, never on a sealed set.

sentences.text: A baker stacks pancakes onto a swaying tower in a busy diner without letting it topple
A sushi chef drops each slice of fish at the perfect moment onto a rolling conveyor belt
A samurai slices flying watermelons tossed into the air at a beach party
A pirate slices flying coconuts in half with his cutlass on a sunny beach
A farmer catches eggs dropping from a henhouse roof in a straw basket
A little girl catches falling snowflakes in a mitten in a quiet mountain village
Drop shiny gemstones into a mine cart so matching gems fuse into bigger jewels
A toy maker combines matching wooden blocks into bigger toys inside a workshop crate
A carnival kid bops sneaky moles popping out of holes at a fairground stand
A castle guard defends the drawbridge from waves of goblins charging out of a dark forest
Two sumo crabs shove each other out of a sandy ring on the beach
A frog crosses a busy country road full of tractors to reach the river
A brave pirate grows his crew by sailing through magic gates on a long river
Two knights duel with foam swords on the deck of a pirate ship
A park ranger puts out the fires scattered across a dry forest valley
A disco robot dances to the beat on a glowing city rooftop
